# AI Voice Sales & Customer Lifecycle Agent

# **AI Voice Sales & Customer Lifecycle Agent**

## **Solution Overview & Engineering Approach**

---

## **1\. Executive Summary**

We are building an autonomous AI voice agent that manages the complete customer lifecycle over telephone calls: outbound sales outreach, inbound query handling, appointment booking and management, customer support, and follow-up engagement.

The system conducts natural voice conversations, maintains persistent memory of every customer interaction, retrieves answers from the company's official knowledge base, and executes business actions (bookings, tickets, CRM updates) — all while operating strictly within configurable business rules, with a complete audit trail of every decision.

Three principles define the engineering approach:

1. **Separation of reasoning and execution.** The language model proposes actions; deterministic application code validates and executes them. The model has no direct ability to modify data or place bookings.  
2. **Platform-generic design.** The engine contains no industry-specific logic. Business rules, customer journey stages, tools, and conversational persona are loaded as configuration ("industry packs"), making the platform reusable across clients and domains without code changes.  
3. **Auditability by construction.** Every decision is recorded with its full context — inputs, retrieved data, rules evaluated, confidence, and outcome — enabling the system to explain any action after the fact.

---

## **2\. Capabilities**

| Function | Capabilities |
| ----- | ----- |
| Sales | Outbound sales calls, inbound call handling, product Q\&A grounded in company documents, objection handling, lead qualification |
| Appointments | Real-time slot search, booking, rescheduling, cancellation, reminder calls, no-show follow-up — with capacity, working hours, holidays, and buffer times enforced |
| Support | Ticket creation, grievance handling, escalation to human agents with full context transfer |
| Lifecycle | Persistent per-customer memory, journey stage tracking, retry and callback management, campaign-based outreach |
| Governance | Do-Not-Contact enforcement, calling-hour compliance, consent tracking, recording disclosure, decision-level audit logs |

---

## **3\. Technology Stack**

| Layer | Technology | Rationale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Backend framework | Python 3.12, FastAPI (async) | Team's established stack; strong async support required for concurrent call handling |
| Database | PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector | Single store for relational data (CRM, scheduling, audit) and vector embeddings (knowledge retrieval); avoids operating a separate vector database |
| Cache / queues | Redis 7 | Session state for live calls, task queues, distributed locks for booking concurrency |
| Background jobs | Celery workers | Post-call processing, campaign dialing, reminders, retries, document ingestion |
| Frontend | React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS | Admin dashboard; team's established stack |
| Telephony | Plivo (primary); Exotel and Twilio adapters | India-focused pricing and DID availability; all providers sit behind a common abstraction layer with automatic failover |
| Speech-to-Text | Deepgram (streaming); Azure Speech fallback | Best-in-class latency and accuracy for telephone-grade audio; Indian English models available |
| Text-to-Speech | ElevenLabs Flash or Azure Neural (streaming) | Sub-300 ms first-byte synthesis, natural voice quality |
| Language models | Claude Sonnet (conversation reasoning and response generation); Claude Haiku (intent classification, summarization, fact extraction) | Two-tier model strategy: the high-capability model is reserved for decision-making; the fast, low-cost model handles high-volume background tasks, reducing cost approximately 10–20× on those workloads |
| Embeddings | OpenAI text-embedding-3-small | Knowledge base semantic search |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on Azure Ubuntu VM; Azure Blob Storage; Azure Key Vault | Deployed in the same region as the telephony provider's India endpoints to minimize audio round-trip latency |
| Observability | Prometheus, Grafana, structured logging (structlog) | Per-stage latency tracking, agent quality metrics, cost monitoring |

All external providers (telephony, STT, TTS, LLM, embeddings) are integrated through internal interface abstractions with configured fallbacks, so any provider can be replaced or failed over without changes to application logic.

## **4\. System Architecture**

**![][image1]**

The system consists of four deployable components:

**Core Platform (modular monolith).** Hosts the decision engine and all business services: conversation management, planning, rule evaluation, tool execution, customer memory, knowledge retrieval, scheduling, CRM, tickets, campaigns, and audit. Implemented as a single FastAPI application with strict internal module boundaries — chosen over microservices because these modules share transactions and context on every conversational turn, and separating them would introduce distributed-system complexity without benefit at target scale.

**Voice Session Service (separate service).** Manages live calls: telephony media streams, streaming speech recognition and synthesis, interruption and silence handling. Deployed separately because its scaling characteristics (I/O-bound audio streaming, WebSocket-heavy) differ from the core platform, and a fault in call handling must not affect the core engine.

**Worker pool.** Celery workers for all asynchronous work: post-call summarization and fact extraction, campaign dialing, reminder and retry scheduling, knowledge document ingestion.

**Admin Dashboard.** React application for operations staff: customer and call management, live call monitoring, rule and knowledge base editing, campaign control, analytics, and audit trail review.

The two services communicate through a single frozen contract — `process_turn(conversation, user_input) → agent_response` — which allows voice-layer and engine development to proceed in parallel and enables additional channels (chat, WhatsApp) to reuse the same engine unchanged.

## **5\. Conversation Processing: The Decision Cycle**

**![][image2]**

Each customer utterance is processed through a fixed twelve-step cycle. Steps are implemented either as deterministic code or as LLM calls; the distinction is deliberate and central to the design. A typical turn requires only two to three LLM calls, which keeps both latency and per-call cost controlled.

**Context assembly** *(deterministic)*. The engine loads the customer profile, extracted facts, summaries of previous conversations, the current conversation history, and the customer's journey stage.

**Intent understanding** *(LLM — Claude Haiku)*. A fast classification call determines the customer's intent and extracts structured entities (dates, products, locations). Speech-recognition confidence from the voice layer is factored in at this stage.

**Knowledge retrieval** *(deterministic)*. For factual queries, the engine performs hybrid search over the knowledge base: pgvector semantic similarity combined with PostgreSQL full-text search, merged by reciprocal rank fusion. Documents outside their configured validity period (e.g., expired promotions) are excluded at query level.

**Candidate action filtering** *(deterministic)*. The tool registry is filtered to actions that are valid in the customer's current journey stage, enabled for the tenant, and permitted for the agent's role. The LLM is only ever presented with this filtered list — actions invalid in the current context are not visible to the model, which structurally eliminates entire categories of erroneous behavior.

**Rule evaluation** *(deterministic)*. All active business rules are evaluated. Rules may block actions, impose prerequisites (e.g., identity verification before account changes), or force escalation. Blocked actions are removed from the candidate list. Rule evaluation contains no LLM involvement and is fully repeatable.

**Action proposal** *(LLM — Claude Sonnet)*. The primary reasoning call. The model receives the conversation context, customer memory, retrieved knowledge, the filtered action list with parameter schemas, and the stage-specific objective. It returns a structured JSON proposal: chosen action, parameters, response draft, and a self-assessed confidence score.

**Confidence gating** *(deterministic)*. The model's self-assessment is adjusted by objective factors — speech-recognition quality, retrieval grounding strength, ambiguity between candidate actions, and repeated clarification attempts — producing a final score mapped to three bands: **high** (proceed to validation), **medium** (do not act; ask a confirming question), **low** (escalate to a human). Thresholds are tenant-configurable.

**Validation** *(deterministic)*. Three mandatory gates before any execution: parameter validation against the tool's JSON Schema; precondition checks against live data (slot existence and capacity, appointment ownership); and idempotency verification to prevent duplicate effects such as double-booking.

**Execution** *(deterministic)*. The action runs within a database transaction where applicable. Slot booking uses row-level locking to guarantee that concurrent calls cannot book the same capacity. Each tool defines a timeout and an explicit failure policy (retry, offer alternative, or escalate).

**Postcondition verification and state transition** *(deterministic)*. The engine verifies the intended effect exists in the database before reporting success. Only then does the customer's journey stage advance. A failed verification is treated as a failed action — success is never reported to the customer without database-level proof.

**Response generation** *(LLM — Claude Sonnet)*. The reply is generated from a grounding context containing only verified execution results and retrieved knowledge passages, with instructions prohibiting any figure, date, price, or time not present in that material. Combined with retrieval-level validity filtering, this constitutes the system's primary defense against fabricated information.

**Decision trace** *(deterministic)*. A complete audit record is persisted asynchronously: input, memory and knowledge references consumed, every rule evaluated with its verdict, the model's proposal and reasoning, validation results, confidence, action taken, prompt versions, model identifiers, token usage, and per-stage latency.

---

## **6\. Core Engine Components**

### **6.1 Tool Registry**

Every executable action is defined by a declarative contract stored in the database, specifying: input schema (JSON Schema), journey stages in which the action is permitted, preconditions verified against live data, postconditions proving successful execution, effects (state transitions, emitted events), failure policy, timeout, and an idempotency key. Actions with irreversible effects (bookings, cancellations, ticket creation) are additionally flagged `requires_confirmation`, which forces an explicit customer confirmation turn before execution.

Contracts are configuration, not code: enabling a tool for a new tenant, adjusting its permitted stages, or integrating an external system (a client's own CRM exposed as an HTTP tool) requires no engine changes, and every tool — internal or external — passes through identical validation and audit machinery.

### **6.2 Rule Engine**

Business policies are authored in YAML, versioned, validated at activation, and evaluated by deterministic code at three checkpoints: before any outbound dial, before any proposed action, and on every turn. Rules emit verdicts — block, require, escalate — and a block cannot be overridden by any other rule or by model reasoning. Standard rule sets ship with the platform (calling policy, retry policy, escalation policy, appointment policy, eligibility); tenants extend or modify them through the dashboard, with full version history and single-action rollback. Every rule evaluation, including non-matches, is written to the decision trace, making questions such as "why was this customer not called" answerable from a single record.

### **6.3 Customer Journey State Machine**

Each customer occupies exactly one journey stage (Lead, Contacted, Qualified, Interested, Appointment Booked, Converted, and others), defined in configuration per industry pack. Each stage carries an objective that is injected into the reasoning prompt, which is how a single engine behaves as a sales agent for a lead and as a support agent for an open ticket. Stage transitions occur only as verified effects of executed tools or explicit signals (e.g., an opt-out request) — the model cannot assert a stage change. Interrupting stages (Call Later, Support Active) suspend and later restore the customer's position in the journey. Every transition is recorded with its trigger, actor, and confidence.

### **6.4 Memory Architecture**

| Memory type | Content | Storage | Written by |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Working | Current conversation turns and extracted entities | Redis (session-scoped) | Live, per turn |
| Episodic | Structured summaries of past conversations: outcome, sentiment, next step | PostgreSQL | Post-call worker (Claude Haiku) |
| Semantic | Extracted customer facts: preferences, objections, pain points, buying intent — each with confidence and source-conversation provenance | PostgreSQL | Post-call extraction (Claude Haiku) |
| Organizational | Company knowledge: brochures, pricing, FAQs, policies, playbooks | PostgreSQL \+ pgvector | Ingestion pipeline |

Facts are append-only with supersede links — a corrected fact retains its history — and supervisors can review or amend the agent's memory through the dashboard. The identifiers of every memory item consulted in a decision are recorded in that decision's trace.

### **6.5 Confidence and Escalation**

Escalation to human agents is triggered either by the low-confidence band or by rule (VIP customers with negative sentiment, legal or payment-dispute indicators, repeated failed interactions, explicit customer request). The escalation form — immediate warm transfer, scheduled human callback, or ticket — is determined by the rule engine. For warm transfers, the system generates a context briefing (customer identity, journey stage, conversation summary, pending items) delivered to the receiving agent's console, and automated outbound contact with that customer is suspended until the escalation is resolved by a human.

---

## **7\. Voice Processing Approach**

The voice layer streams call audio to Deepgram for continuous transcription and streams generated replies through TTS, with end-of-turn detection combining transcription finality, voice-activity detection, and a configurable silence threshold. The end-to-end latency target is approximately **1.2 seconds** from the customer's last word to the first audio of the reply, achieved through: full streaming at every stage, speculative early processing of stable transcripts, sentence-level incremental synthesis, pre-generated audio for fixed phrases (disclosure, greetings, acknowledgments), and co-located deployment with the telephony provider's regional endpoints. Interruption handling (barge-in) halts agent audio within 150 ms of detected customer speech and informs the engine which portion of the reply was actually delivered. Full detail: *Voice Pipeline Design*.

---

## **8\. Platform Genericity and Multi-Tenancy**

The engine is domain-agnostic. All business-specific behavior — journey stages, rules, enabled tools, conversational persona, knowledge content — is delivered as an **industry pack**: a versioned configuration bundle imported per tenant. Onboarding a new client or vertical is a configuration exercise, not a development project. The data model is multi-tenant throughout (tenant-scoped rows, repository-level filtering, PostgreSQL row-level security as defense in depth), and per-tenant provider selection is supported (e.g., different telephony vendors per client).

---

## **9\. Safety, Compliance, and Quality Assurance**

**Compliance controls** are structural where possible: Do-Not-Contact is evaluated as the first, terminal rule before every dial with no bypassing code path; recording disclosure is enforced by the call session's state machine; consent is tracked in an append-only ledger with evidence references; PII is masked at the logging layer so raw identifiers cannot reach log files; and the model is never granted tools for destructive or privileged operations. Regulatory alignment covers TRAI/TCCCPR telemarketing requirements and DPDP Act data-protection principles. Full detail: *Compliance, Security & Audit Design*.

**Quality assurance** for agent behavior goes beyond conventional testing: a scripted conversation test suite asserts correct engine behavior across happy paths, failure branches, rule triggers, and adversarial inputs; a curated golden set of \~100 human-approved conversation turns is re-evaluated on every prompt or model change with human review of any behavioral diff; and production monitoring tracks escalation rate, blocked-action rate, grounding failures, and per-stage latency. Business KPIs (connection rate, conversion rate, appointments booked and completed, resolution times) and agent KPIs (action accuracy, latency, escalation rate) are computed from the same event and trace data. Full detail: *Deployment & Testing Strategy*.

# Architecture & Data Design

# **Architecture & Data Design**

---

## **1\. Design Principles**

1. **Domain-agnostic core.** Nothing in the engine knows about "insurance" or "clinics". All domain behavior lives in **Industry Packs**: config bundles containing tools config, rules YAML, state machine definition, prompts, and knowledge documents. Deploying for a new vertical \= new pack, zero engine code changes.  
2. **The LLM never executes tools.** The LLM proposes; the Planner validates against the tool contract and Rule Engine, then the Executor runs it. (Detailed in the Solution Overview & Engineering Approach document.)  
3. **Provider abstraction everywhere it hurts.** Telephony, STT, TTS, LLM, and embeddings are all behind interfaces with swappable adapters. Full abstraction layer (not thin adapter) — per full-scope decision.  
4. **Everything auditable.** Every decision step emits an audit event with inputs, retrieved context, rules evaluated, and confidence. Explainability is a query over these events, not a reconstruction.  
5. **Tenant-ready from day one.** Single-tenant deployments are just multi-tenant with one row in `tenants`. Every table carries `tenant_id`.  
6. **Config over code.** States, rules, tools, prompts, calling policies — all data, editable via admin API without redeploy.

## **2\. High-Level Architecture**

**![][image3]**

### **2.1 Service Boundaries (what runs as what)**

| Unit | Deployment | Why separate / why not |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Core Platform** | 1 FastAPI app (modular monolith), N replicas | All engine modules share transactions, memory, and the tool registry. Splitting them buys nothing at this scale and costs distributed-transaction pain. |
| **Voice Session Service** | Separate FastAPI/asyncio service | Different scaling profile (1 process ≈ N concurrent media streams, CPU-bound audio, WebSocket-heavy). Must be deployable close to telephony region. Crashes must not take down the core. |
| **Worker Pool** | Celery (or ARQ) workers | Post-call summarization, campaign dialing, reminder scheduling, document ingestion, retry timers. |
| **Admin Dashboard** | React 18 \+ Vite \+ Tailwind SPA | Your standard stack. |
| **Postgres \+ pgvector** | Managed (Azure Flexible Server) or VM | One database for relational \+ vector. No MongoDB — CRM/state/audit data is relational; conversation payloads fit JSONB. |
| **Redis** | Single instance \+ persistence | Session state (working memory), queues, rate limits, distributed locks (slot booking). |
| **Object storage** | Azure Blob / S3-compatible | Call recordings, raw transcripts, uploaded knowledge documents. |

### **2.2 Provider Abstraction Layer (full scope)**

Each external capability is a Python protocol with adapters registered in config:

providers:  
  telephony:  { active: plivo,   fallback: exotel }  
  stt:        { active: deepgram, fallback: azure\_stt }  
  tts:        { active: elevenlabs, fallback: azure\_tts }  
  llm:        { planner: claude-sonnet, summarizer: claude-haiku, fallback: gpt-4o }  
  embeddings: { active: openai-3-small }

Interfaces (usage detail in the Voice Pipeline Design document):

* `TelephonyProvider`: `originate_call`, `answer`, `hangup`, `transfer`, `start_recording`, `send_dtmf`, webhook normalization → canonical `CallEvent`  
* `STTProvider`: `stream_transcribe(audio_stream) → async iterator[TranscriptEvent]` (partial \+ final)  
* `TTSProvider`: `stream_synthesize(text_stream) → async iterator[AudioChunk]`  
* `LLMProvider`: `complete`, `stream_complete`, tool-call-shaped outputs normalized to internal schema  
* `EmbeddingProvider`: `embed(texts) → vectors`

Canonical event/DTO models mean the engine never sees provider-specific payloads. Fallback routing: if the active provider errors ≥ threshold within a window, the circuit breaker flips to fallback and raises an ops alert.

| Layer | Choice | Notes |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Core API | **Python 3.12 \+ FastAPI** | Your stack; async-first throughout |
| Voice service | FastAPI \+ `asyncio` \+ `websockets` | Media streaming over WS |
| Workers | **Celery \+ Redis** (or ARQ if you prefer pure-async) | Scheduled \+ queued jobs |
| DB | **PostgreSQL 16 \+ pgvector** | Relational \+ embeddings in one store |
| ORM / migrations | SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async) \+ Alembic |  |
| Cache/queues/locks | **Redis 7** |  |
| Object storage | Azure Blob | Recordings, docs |
| Telephony | **Plivo** (primary), Exotel adapter (India DID \+ TRAI compliance), Twilio adapter (global) | Behind abstraction layer |
| STT | **Deepgram** streaming (primary), Azure STT fallback | Best latency/accuracy for telephone audio; Indian-English models |
| TTS | **ElevenLabs Flash / Azure Neural** | Streaming, \<300ms first-byte |
| LLM | **Claude Sonnet** (planner/conversation), **Claude Haiku** (summarization, extraction, classification) | Cheap model for high-volume background jobs |
| Embeddings | OpenAI text-embedding-3-small or voyage-3 | 1536-dim default |
| Frontend | React 18 \+ Vite \+ Tailwind | Your stack |
| Realtime dashboard | WebSocket (FastAPI) | Live call monitor |
| Deploy | Docker Compose on Azure Ubuntu VM (PM2 optional for node-less setup → prefer systemd/compose) | Kubernetes not needed at this scale |
| Observability | structlog \+ Prometheus \+ Grafana; audit events in Postgres |  |

    │   ├── rules/                     \# business rules  
    │   ├── tools.yaml                 \# enabled tools \+ param overrides  
    │   ├── prompts/                   \# persona, pitch style, objection handling  
    │   └── knowledge/                 \# seed documents  
    └── example\_clinic/

---

## **5\. Database Design (PostgreSQL 16 \+ pgvector)**

Conventions: every table has `id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, `created_at/updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ`. Indexes noted inline. All FKs implicit by name.

### **5.1 Platform & Identity**

tenants (  
  id, name, slug UNIQUE, industry\_pack TEXT,        \-- which pack is active  
  timezone TEXT DEFAULT 'Asia/Kolkata',  
  settings JSONB DEFAULT '{}',                       \-- provider overrides, locale  
  status TEXT CHECK (status IN ('active','suspended'))  
)

users (                                              \-- dashboard/human users  
  id, tenant\_id, email UNIQUE(tenant\_id,email), password\_hash,  
  full\_name, role TEXT,                              \-- FK-ish to roles.name  
  is\_active BOOL, last\_login\_at  
)

roles (  
  id, tenant\_id, name,                               \-- admin, supervisor, agent, analyst  
  permissions JSONB                                  \-- \["customers:read","rules:write",...\]  
)

api\_keys (  
  id, tenant\_id, name, key\_hash, scopes JSONB, expires\_at, last\_used\_at  
)

### **5.2 CRM & Customer Memory**

customers (  
  id, tenant\_id,  
  full\_name, phone TEXT NOT NULL, phone\_normalized TEXT,   \-- E.164  
  email, location TEXT, region\_code TEXT,  
  preferred\_language TEXT DEFAULT 'en',  
  preferred\_contact\_start TIME, preferred\_contact\_end TIME,  
  current\_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'lead',              \-- FSM state (validated vs pack)  
  lead\_source TEXT, priority\_score NUMERIC DEFAULT 0,  
  assigned\_executive\_id UUID NULL,  
  tags TEXT\[\], external\_ref TEXT,                          \-- link to client's own CRM  
  UNIQUE (tenant\_id, phone\_normalized)  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, current\_state), (tenant\_id, priority\_score DESC), GIN(tags)

customer\_facts (                       \-- SEMANTIC MEMORY: extracted, structured  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id,  
  category TEXT,                       \-- pain\_point | objection | preference |  
                                       \-- buying\_intent | decision\_maker | product\_interest  
  key TEXT, value JSONB,  
  confidence NUMERIC,                  \-- extraction confidence 0..1  
  source\_conversation\_id UUID NULL,    \-- provenance  
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',        \-- active | superseded | retracted  
  superseded\_by UUID NULL  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, customer\_id, category, status)

customer\_product\_interest (  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id, product\_ref TEXT,  
  interest\_level TEXT,                 \-- interested | purchased | rejected  
  noted\_at, source\_conversation\_id  
)

state\_transitions (  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id,  
  from\_state TEXT, to\_state TEXT,  
  trigger TEXT,                        \-- tool name / rule / manual / system  
  tool\_execution\_id UUID NULL,  
  actor TEXT,                          \-- 'agent' | 'human:\<user\_id\>' | 'system'  
  confidence NUMERIC, reason TEXT, occurred\_at TIMESTAMPTZ  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, customer\_id, occurred\_at DESC)

### **5.3 Conversations, Calls & Episodic Memory**

conversations (                        \-- channel-agnostic container  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id,  
  channel TEXT,                        \-- voice | chat | whatsapp(future) | email(future)  
  direction TEXT,                      \-- inbound | outbound  
  status TEXT,                         \-- active | completed | abandoned  
  started\_at, ended\_at,  
  summary TEXT,                        \-- EPISODIC MEMORY: post-call summary  
  outcome TEXT,                        \-- booked | callback\_requested | not\_interested | ...  
  sentiment TEXT, intent\_labels TEXT\[\],  
  campaign\_id UUID NULL  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, customer\_id, started\_at DESC)

messages (  
  id, tenant\_id, conversation\_id,  
  role TEXT,                           \-- customer | agent | system | tool  
  content TEXT,  
  audio\_offset\_ms INT NULL,            \-- position in recording  
  tool\_execution\_id UUID NULL,  
  metadata JSONB, created\_at  
)  
\-- INDEX: (conversation\_id, created\_at)

calls (                                \-- telephony-specific facts for a conversation  
  id, tenant\_id, conversation\_id, customer\_id,  
  provider TEXT, provider\_call\_id TEXT,  
  from\_number, to\_number,  
  status TEXT,                         \-- queued|ringing|answered|busy|no\_answer|failed|completed  
  answered\_at, ended\_at, duration\_seconds INT,  
  hangup\_cause TEXT, recording\_url TEXT, transcript\_url TEXT,  
  disclosure\_played BOOL DEFAULT false,  
  retry\_of\_call\_id UUID NULL, retry\_reason TEXT,  
  cost NUMERIC NULL  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, customer\_id, created\_at DESC), (provider, provider\_call\_id)

callback\_requests (                    \-- "call me later"  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id, requested\_for TIMESTAMPTZ,  
  source\_conversation\_id, status TEXT, \-- pending | completed | cancelled  
  fulfilled\_by\_call\_id UUID NULL  
)

### **5.4 Scheduling Engine**

centres (  
  id, tenant\_id, name, address, city, region\_code,  
  lat NUMERIC, lng NUMERIC, phone, timezone,  
  is\_active BOOL  
)

executives (                           \-- bookable humans  
  id, tenant\_id, centre\_id, full\_name, email, phone,  
  specialties TEXT\[\], is\_active BOOL  
)

working\_hours (  
  id, tenant\_id,  
  owner\_type TEXT, owner\_id UUID,      \-- centre | executive  
  day\_of\_week INT,                     \-- 0-6  
  start\_time TIME, end\_time TIME  
)

holidays (  
  id, tenant\_id, owner\_type, owner\_id NULL,  \-- NULL \= tenant-wide  
  date DATE, name TEXT  
)

slot\_policies (  
  id, tenant\_id, centre\_id NULL,  
  slot\_duration\_min INT, buffer\_before\_min INT, buffer\_after\_min INT,  
  max\_parallel INT,                    \-- capacity per slot  
  booking\_horizon\_days INT, min\_notice\_hours INT  
)

appointments (  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id, centre\_id, executive\_id NULL,  
  starts\_at TIMESTAMPTZ, ends\_at TIMESTAMPTZ,  
  status TEXT,                         \-- booked|rescheduled|cancelled|completed|no\_show  
  booked\_via TEXT,                     \-- agent | dashboard | api  
  source\_conversation\_id UUID NULL,  
  reschedule\_of UUID NULL, cancel\_reason TEXT,  
  reminder\_state JSONB DEFAULT '{}'    \-- {t24h: sent, t2h: pending}  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, centre\_id, starts\_at), (tenant\_id, customer\_id),  
\--        (tenant\_id, executive\_id, starts\_at)  
\-- Slot availability \= computed (working\_hours − holidays − appointments  
\--   respecting slot\_policies), never materialized. Booking uses  
\--   SELECT ... FOR UPDATE \+ capacity check in one transaction (+ Redis lock).

### **5.5 Knowledge (RAG)**

knowledge\_documents (  
  id, tenant\_id, title, doc\_type TEXT,   \-- brochure|faq|pricing|policy|promo|playbook|sop|compliance  
  source\_uri TEXT,                       \-- blob path  
  status TEXT,                           \-- processing | ready | failed  
  version INT, effective\_from DATE NULL, effective\_to DATE NULL,  \-- promos expire  
  metadata JSONB  
)

knowledge\_chunks (  
  id, tenant\_id, document\_id,  
  chunk\_index INT, content TEXT,  
  embedding VECTOR(1536),  
  token\_count INT, metadata JSONB        \-- headings, page, product refs  
)  
\-- INDEX: HNSW (embedding vector\_cosine\_ops), (tenant\_id, document\_id)  
\-- Hybrid search: pgvector cosine \+ tsvector GIN on content, RRF-merged (see Solution Overview, Section 5\)

### **5.6 Engine Configuration (tools, rules, states, prompts)**

tool\_definitions (                       \-- the TOOL REGISTRY (contract: Solution Overview 6.1)  
  id, tenant\_id, name UNIQUE(tenant\_id,name), description,  
  category TEXT,                         \-- sales|scheduling|support|utility  
  input\_schema JSONB,                    \-- JSON Schema: required/optional params  
  preconditions JSONB,                   \-- declarative checks (Solution Overview 6.1)  
  postconditions JSONB,  
  failure\_policy JSONB,                  \-- retry, fallback tool, escalate  
  requires\_confirmation BOOL,            \-- read back to customer before executing  
  permission\_level TEXT,                 \-- which roles / agent may invoke  
  implementation TEXT,                   \-- python path of builtin, or 'http' for external  
  http\_config JSONB NULL,                \-- for external tool endpoints  
  is\_enabled BOOL  
)

rule\_sets (  
  id, tenant\_id, name, category TEXT,    \-- calling\_policy|retry|dnd|escalation|appointment|eligibility  
  yaml\_source TEXT,                      \-- authored YAML (see Solution Overview 6.2)  
  compiled JSONB,                        \-- parsed/validated form the engine evaluates  
  version INT, is\_active BOOL, activated\_by UUID, activated\_at  
)  
\-- history kept: new version \= new row; is\_active flips

state\_machine\_defs (  
  id, tenant\_id, version INT, is\_active BOOL,  
  definition JSONB                       \-- states, allowed transitions, entry actions  
)

prompt\_templates (  
  id, tenant\_id, name, purpose TEXT,     \-- persona|planner|summarizer|objection|pitch  
  template TEXT, model\_hint TEXT, version INT, is\_active BOOL  
)

### **5.7 Support, Campaigns, Consent**

tickets (  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id, conversation\_id NULL,  
  subject, description, category TEXT, priority TEXT,  
  status TEXT,                           \-- open|in\_progress|resolved|escalated|closed  
  assigned\_to UUID NULL, resolution TEXT, resolved\_at,  
  sla\_due\_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL  
)

escalations (  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id, conversation\_id, ticket\_id NULL,  
  reason TEXT,                           \-- low\_confidence|failed\_interactions|legal|vip|payment\_dispute|customer\_request  
  trigger\_rule TEXT NULL, confidence NUMERIC NULL,  
  status TEXT,                           \-- pending|accepted|resolved  
  assigned\_to UUID NULL, transferred\_call\_id UUID NULL  
)

campaigns (  
  id, tenant\_id, name, status,           \-- draft|running|paused|completed  
  audience\_filter JSONB,                 \-- CRM query definition  
  pack\_prompt\_override UUID NULL,  
  schedule JSONB,                        \-- windows, pacing (calls/hour), start/end dates  
  stats JSONB                            \-- denormalized counters  
)

campaign\_targets (  
  id, tenant\_id, campaign\_id, customer\_id,  
  status TEXT,                           \-- pending|calling|done|failed|excluded  
  attempts INT, last\_attempt\_at, exclusion\_reason TEXT  
)

consent\_records (                        \-- append-only consent ledger  
  id, tenant\_id, customer\_id,  
  consent\_type TEXT,                     \-- calls|recording|marketing|data\_processing  
  granted BOOL, channel TEXT, evidence\_uri TEXT,  \-- recording clip / form ref  
  recorded\_at TIMESTAMPTZ  
)

dnc\_list (                               \-- Do Not Contact  
  id, tenant\_id, phone\_normalized, customer\_id NULL,  
  scope TEXT,                            \-- all|marketing|voice  
  source TEXT,                           \-- customer\_request|regulator|import  
  added\_at, expires\_at NULL  
)  
\-- INDEX: UNIQUE (tenant\_id, phone\_normalized, scope)

### **5.8 Audit & Analytics**

decision\_traces (                        \-- EXPLAINABILITY core (one per planner cycle)  
  id, tenant\_id, conversation\_id, customer\_id, turn\_index INT,  
  input\_text TEXT,  
  retrieved\_memory JSONB,                \-- fact/summary ids \+ snippets used  
  retrieved\_chunks JSONB,                \-- knowledge chunk ids \+ scores  
  rules\_evaluated JSONB,                 \-- \[{rule, result, reason}\]  
  planner\_reasoning TEXT,  
  proposed\_tool TEXT NULL, tool\_params JSONB NULL,  
  validation\_result JSONB,               \-- pre/postcondition outcomes  
  confidence NUMERIC, confidence\_band TEXT,   \-- high|medium|low  
  action\_taken TEXT,                     \-- executed|clarified|escalated|blocked  
  state\_transition\_id UUID NULL,  
  latency\_ms INT, model\_used TEXT, tokens JSONB,  
  created\_at  
)  
\-- INDEX: (tenant\_id, conversation\_id, turn\_index), (tenant\_id, created\_at)  
\-- Partition by month at scale.

tool\_executions (  
  id, tenant\_id, decision\_trace\_id, tool\_name,  
  input JSONB, output JSONB, status TEXT,   \-- success|failed|blocked  
  error TEXT NULL, duration\_ms INT, created\_at  
)

audit\_events (                           \-- generic security/admin audit  
  id, tenant\_id, actor TEXT, action TEXT, resource\_type, resource\_id,  
  before JSONB NULL, after JSONB NULL, ip TEXT, created\_at  
)

analytics\_events (                       \-- append-only event stream for KPIs  
  id, tenant\_id, event\_type TEXT,        \-- call\_placed|call\_connected|appointment\_booked|...  
  customer\_id NULL, conversation\_id NULL, properties JSONB, occurred\_at  
)  
\-- KPIs (connection rate, conversion, tool accuracy, escalation rate, CSAT,  
\-- hallucination flags) are SQL aggregations / materialized views over this  
\-- \+ decision\_traces. No separate analytics DB in v1.

## **6\. Memory Architecture → Storage Mapping**

| PRD Memory | Storage | Written by | Read by planner as |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Working** (current conversation) | Redis hash per session (`session:{conv_id}`): rolling turn window, extracted slots, current intent. TTL \= call \+ 1h. Flushed to `messages` continuously. | Conversation Manager, live | Full context block |
| **Episodic** (past conversations) | `conversations.summary` \+ `outcome`, `sentiment` | Post-call worker (Haiku summarization) | Last N summaries (default 5\) |
| **Semantic** (profile, facts, preferences) | `customers` \+ `customer_facts` \+ `customer_product_interest` | Post-call extraction job; also live extraction for critical facts (e.g., "call me after 6pm") | Structured profile block |
| **Organizational** (shared knowledge) | `knowledge_chunks` (pgvector) | Ingestion worker | Top-k retrieved chunks |

**Full pipeline (Observe → Extract → Summarize → Update → Audit):**

1. **Observe** — every turn appended to `messages`; working memory updated in Redis.  
2. **Extract** (post-call, \+ inline for critical facts) — Haiku pass over transcript → candidate facts with confidence, category, provenance. Facts below confidence threshold are stored as `status='candidate'` for human review rather than discarded.  
3. **Summarize** — structured summary (outcome, objections, sentiment, next-step) → `conversations.summary`.  
4. **Update** — facts merged into `customer_facts` with supersede logic (new value ≠ old → old row `superseded`, linked via `superseded_by`; never destructive). Profile fields (preferred time, language) promoted when confidence ≥ threshold.  
5. **Audit** — memory-write events into `audit_events`; every planner read logs the exact fact/summary IDs consumed into `decision_traces.retrieved_memory` — this is what makes "which memories influenced this decision" a single query.

---

## **7\. Multi-Tenancy & Industry Packs**

* **Isolation:** shared schema, `tenant_id` on every row, enforced by a repository-layer tenant filter (every query goes through repositories; raw session access is lint-blocked). Postgres RLS enabled as defense-in-depth for `customers`, `customer_facts`, `consent_records`, `dnc_list`.  
* **Pack loading:** `tenants.industry_pack` names a pack; on activation, pack YAMLs are imported into `state_machine_defs`, `rule_sets`, `tool_definitions`, `prompt_templates` as versioned rows. Runtime reads only from DB — packs are seeders, not runtime dependencies. Editing via dashboard just creates new versions.  
* **Per-tenant provider overrides** in `tenants.settings` (e.g., one tenant on Exotel, another on Plivo; different TTS voice).  
* **Single-tenant deployment** (your likely v1) \= one tenant row. Nothing else changes.

---

## **8\. Key Architectural Decisions (summary)**

| \# | Decision | Rationale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| AD-1 | Modular monolith \+ separate voice service | Latency/scaling isolation for media; transactional simplicity for engine |
| AD-2 | Postgres \+ pgvector only (no MongoDB) | Data is relational; JSONB covers flexible payloads; one DB to operate |
| AD-3 | Full provider abstraction with fallback routing | Full-scope requirement; also de-risks India telephony vendor churn |
| AD-4 | Slot availability computed, never materialized | Eliminates slot-table sync bugs; booking correctness via row locks |
| AD-5 | All engine config (states/rules/tools/prompts) in versioned DB rows | Domain-agnostic platform; edit without redeploy; full audit history |
| AD-6 | `decision_traces` as first-class table | Explainability is a query, not log spelunking |
| AD-7 | Facts are append-only with supersede links | Memory is auditable and reversible; no silent overwrites |
| AD-8 | Haiku-class model for all background LLM jobs | 10–20x cost reduction on summarization/extraction volume |

# Workflow Chart

# API Specification

# **API Specification**

---

## **1\. The Basics (Read This First)**

**Base URL:** `https://<your-domain>/api/v1`

**Format:** Everything is JSON in, JSON out. Timestamps are ISO-8601 with timezone (`2026-07-18T10:30:00+05:30`). IDs are UUIDs.

**Who calls this API:**

* The **React dashboard** (humans managing the system)  
* The **Voice Session Service** (the phone-call handler — it mainly calls `process_turn`)  
* The **telephony provider** (Plivo/Exotel sends us call events via webhooks)  
* **External systems** of a client (their CRM syncing customers, for example)

### **Authentication — two kinds**

| Kind | Used by | How |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **JWT (login token)** | Dashboard users | `POST /auth/login` with email \+ password → returns an access token (30 min) \+ refresh token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| **API key** | Services and integrations | Created in the dashboard with limited scopes (e.g., "can read customers, can't edit rules"). Sent as `X-API-Key: <key>` |

Every request runs as one **tenant** (business). The tenant is inside the token/key — you never pass tenant\_id manually, and you can never see another tenant's data.

**Permissions:** every user has a role (`admin`, `supervisor`, `agent`, `analyst`), and every endpoint declares what role it needs. Trying something above your role → `403`.

### **Errors — one shape everywhere**

{  
  "error": {  
    "code": "SLOT\_NOT\_AVAILABLE",  
    "message": "The requested slot is no longer available.",  
    "details": { "requested\_slot": "2026-07-18T10:30:00+05:30" },  
    "request\_id": "req\_8f3a..."  
  }  
}

`request_id` appears in our logs too — quote it when reporting a problem. Standard HTTP codes: `400` bad input · `401` not logged in · `403` not allowed · `404` not found · `409` conflict (e.g., double booking) · `422` validation failed · `429` too many requests · `500` our bug.

### **Lists — one pattern everywhere**

All list endpoints accept `?page=1&page_size=25&sort=-created_at` plus endpoint-specific filters, and return:

{ "items": \[...\], "page": 1, "page\_size": 25, "total": 312 }

---

## **2\. The Conversation API (the engine's front door)**

### **`POST /conversations/{id}/turns` — process one turn**

This is **the** endpoint — everything else is management around it. The voice service (or a chat client) calls it every time the customer says something.

Request:

{  
  "user\_input": "Saturday morning works for me",  
  "channel": "voice",  
  "input\_metadata": { "stt\_confidence": 0.91, "interrupted": false }  
}

Response:

{  
  "response\_text": "Great\! Just to confirm — Saturday July 18th, 10:30 AM at our Vapi centre. Shall I book it?",  
  "response\_segments": \["Great\!", "Just to confirm — Saturday July 18th, 10:30 AM at our Vapi centre.", "Shall I book it?"\],  
  "action": "confirm",  
  "executed\_tools": \[\],  
  "state\_changed\_to": null,  
  "escalation": null,  
  "end\_call": false,  
  "trace\_id": "9d2c..."  
}

`response_segments` exists so the voice layer can start speaking sentence 1 while the rest is still being processed — this is a latency trick, explained in the Voice Pipeline doc.

### **Other conversation endpoints**

| Method & path | What it does | Who uses it |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `POST /conversations` | Start a conversation (body: customer\_id or phone, channel, direction) | Voice service, chat |
| `POST /conversations/{id}/end` | Close it (body: reason). Triggers the post-call pipeline: summary, fact extraction, memory update | Voice service |
| `GET /conversations/{id}` | Full detail: messages, tools run, outcome, summary | Dashboard |
| `GET /conversations` | List/filter by customer, channel, outcome, date | Dashboard |
| `GET /conversations/{id}/messages` | Just the transcript | Dashboard |

## **3\. Customers (CRM)**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `POST /customers` | Create a customer (name, phone required; the rest optional) |
| `GET /customers/{id}` | Full profile including current journey stage |
| `GET /customers` | List with filters: `?state=interested&tag=vip&search=sharma&language=hi` |
| `PATCH /customers/{id}` | Edit profile fields |
| `DELETE /customers/{id}` | Soft-delete (kept for audit, excluded from everything) |
| `GET /customers/lookup?phone=+91...` | Find by phone — used on inbound calls to recognize the caller |
| `POST /customers/import` | Bulk import from CSV (returns a job id; see §12) |

### **The customer's memory and journey**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `GET /customers/{id}/facts` | Everything the AI has learned: pain points, objections, preferences — each with confidence and which conversation it came from |
| `PATCH /customers/{id}/facts/{fact_id}` | Correct or retract a fact (humans can fix the AI's memory) |
| `GET /customers/{id}/timeline` | The full story in order: calls, stage changes, appointments, tickets |
| `GET /customers/{id}/state-history` | Just the journey stage changes, with what triggered each |
| `POST /customers/{id}/state` | Manually move a customer's stage (body: `to_state`, `reason`) — supervisor only, recorded as a manual transition |

## **4\. Scheduling & Appointments**

### **Finding slots**

`GET /scheduling/slots?centre_id=...&from=2026-07-18&to=2026-07-21&executive_id=(optional)`

Returns real, bookable slots — already accounting for working hours, holidays, buffer times, capacity, and existing bookings:

{ "slots": \[  
    { "starts\_at": "2026-07-18T10:30:00+05:30", "ends\_at": "...", "capacity\_left": 2 },  
    { "starts\_at": "2026-07-18T11:30:00+05:30", "ends\_at": "...", "capacity\_left": 1 }  
\]}

This same query is what the AI's booking tool uses internally — dashboard and agent always see identical availability.

### **Appointments**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `POST /appointments` | Book (customer\_id, centre\_id, starts\_at). Returns `409 SLOT_NOT_AVAILABLE` if taken in the meantime |
| `PATCH /appointments/{id}/reschedule` | Move to a new slot (old one is released atomically) |
| `POST /appointments/{id}/cancel` | Cancel with reason |
| `POST /appointments/{id}/complete` | Mark attended / no-show (feeds the journey stage) |
| `GET /appointments` | List/filter by centre, customer, date, status |

### **Setup (admin)**

CRUD endpoints, all following the same pattern (`POST`/`GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`):

`/centres` · `/executives` · `/working-hours` · `/holidays` · `/slot-policies` (slot length, buffers, capacity, how far ahead booking is allowed)

---

## **5\. Knowledge Base (what the AI can quote)**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `POST /knowledge/documents` | Upload (multipart file or raw text) \+ metadata: type (`faq/pricing/policy/promo/...`), and optional `effective_from/to` dates. Processing is async — returns a job id |
| `GET /knowledge/documents` | List with processing status (`processing / ready / failed`) |
| `GET /knowledge/documents/{id}` | Detail \+ its chunks |
| `PATCH /knowledge/documents/{id}` | Update metadata / expiry dates |
| `DELETE /knowledge/documents/{id}` | Remove (its content immediately stops being retrievable) |
| `POST /knowledge/search` | Test retrieval by hand: `{ "query": "cancellation charges" }` → the exact chunks \+ scores the AI would see. Essential for debugging "why did the AI say that?" |

The `effective_from/to` dates are how promotions safely expire: after the date passes, the content is automatically excluded from every search.

## **6\. Engine Configuration**

### **Rules**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `GET /rules` | All rule sets with active version numbers |
| `GET /rules/{name}` | The YAML of the active version |
| `PUT /rules/{name}` | Submit new YAML → validated → saved as a **new version** (not yet live) |
| `POST /rules/{name}/activate` | Make a version live (body: `version`). Rollback \= activate the older version |
| `POST /rules/{name}/test` | Dry-run: send a sample situation, get back which rules would fire and the verdicts — test before going live |
| `GET /rules/{name}/versions` | Full history: who changed what, when |

### **Tools**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `GET /tools` | The registry: every tool, enabled or not, its contract |
| `PATCH /tools/{name}` | Enable/disable, edit settings (e.g., turn `requires_confirmation` on) |
| `POST /tools` | Register an external HTTP tool (their endpoint \+ contract) |
| `POST /tools/{name}/test` | Dry-run the validation pipeline with sample params — see exactly which check would fail, without executing |

### **States, prompts, packs**

| Method & path | What it does |
| ----- | ----- |
| `GET /state-machine` / `PUT /state-machine` | View / update the journey definition (versioned, validated on save) |
| `GET /prompts` / `PUT /prompts/{name}` | View / edit persona and task prompts (versioned) |
| `POST /packs/{name}/apply` | Load an industry pack into this tenant (imports its states, rules, tools, prompts as new versions) |
